title: Xi’s Military Purges Make US Deterrence More Urgent
gist: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi argues that Xi's purges have emptied China's Central Military Commission, strengthening Xi's control while weakening readiness, and that this freer hand adds Taiwan risk and makes US deterrence more urgent (truncated excerpt).

insights.claim: Of the seven members chosen for China's Central Military Commission in 2022, only Xi Jinping and one general remain active.
insights.speaker: Raja Krishnamoorthi
insights.so_what: Unprecedented turnover at the top of the PLA is a key indicator for Chinese military risk assessment.

insights.claim: Days before Xi met Trump in Washington last month, Beijing formally expelled Gen. Zhang Youxia, Xi's longtime ally, and Gen. Liu Zhenli, former chief of the Joint Staff Department.
insights.speaker: Raja Krishnamoorthi
insights.so_what: Purges continued even alongside summit diplomacy.

insights.claim: Per Reuters-cited analysts, removal of senior commanders and protégés strengthens Xi's grip on the PLA while weakening near-term readiness.
insights.speaker: Raja Krishnamoorthi
insights.so_what: Near-term operational risk may fall even as decision-making becomes more centralized.

insights.claim: With more of the decision on invading Taiwan, a blockade or other aggression resting on Xi alone, the freer hand adds risk, so US deterrence is more urgent.
insights.speaker: Raja Krishnamoorthi
insights.so_what: Argues for stronger US deterrence posture; tail-risk for Taiwan-exposed assets.
